title: 12 States Push Back on New Mexico in Oracle Data Center Pipeline Fight
key_facts: Attorneys general of 12 states asked federal regulators (FERC) to authorize a gas pipeline needed to power an Oracle data center in New Mexico, in an Oct. 14 letter.
The 17.8-mile Green Chile Project in Doña Ana County would carry up to 400 million cubic feet of gas a day for Project Jupiter, a data-center campus Oracle is developing to serve OpenAI.
The states argue that FERC does not approve data centers and has no authority to regulate them, so it need not review the data center's environmental effects.
New Mexico argues FERC must consider the environmental effects of both pipeline and data center.
They fear FERC's treatment could set a precedent for similar gas-fed data center projects.
Signatories: West Virginia, Alaska, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Louisiana, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Ohio and South Carolina.
quote_evidence: The attorneys general of 12 states have asked federal regulators to authorize construction of a natural gas pipeline needed to power an Oracle Corp. data center in New Mexico, arguing that a broader environmental review could complicate similar projects across the country.
They believe that FERC's treatment of the Green Chile Project could establish a regulatory approach that gets applied to similar gas-fed data center developments elsewhere.
why_it_matters_hint: A local pipeline fight is becoming a national test of how gas-powered data centers get approved.
